name: East Finchley & Fortis Green
why: Small mixed secondaries: The Archer Academy (818 on two sites) and Bishop Douglass (968, Catholic). Several one-class-per-year primaries.

name: Rotherhithe & Surrey Docks
why: Riverside village feel with Redriff Primary (456, Outstanding) and Southwark Park. Small Catholic schools in both phases: St Joseph's (213) and St John's (240) primaries, St Michael's Catholic College (948). The Charter School Bermondsey has only 497 pupils.

name: Crouch End & Hornsey
why: Village feel, two Outstanding 1-form primaries (Weston Park 232, St Aidan's 217) and small secondaries: St Aloysius' (341, Catholic, now mixed) and City of London Academy Highgate Hill (641). Trains from Hornsey and Harringay run straight to Moorgate.

name: Blackheath & Lee
why: Blackheath village and the Heath. St Matthew Academy is a Catholic school for ages 4–16 rated Outstanding in every area (March 2025), so both children could attend. Four 1-form primaries.

name: Friern Barnet & Whetstone
why: Cheaper and quieter. Friern Barnet School has only 591 pupils; two 1-form primaries (Catholic and CofE).

name: Wanstead & Woodford
why: Village high street, Wanstead Park and Epping Forest, family nearby. Small primaries, but both secondaries are large (1,434 and 1,603).

name: Walthamstow
why: Lively and creative (Village, market, Blackhorse Road), next to the Wetlands and Lloyd Park, close to family. Several primaries under 200 pupils, but most secondaries are around 900–1,200.

name: Beckenham
why: Suburban and green, with a cluster of Outstanding primaries (St Mary's Catholic, Clare House, Harris Beckenham Green). Secondaries are large academies, and the commute is the longest in London.

name: Buckhurst Hill & Loughton
why: Most house for the money, right on Epping Forest. Mid-sized schools; Essex runs its own admissions.

name: East Dulwich & Herne Hill
why: Best neighbourhood life, but over budget and the only mixed secondary nearby is large (1,389).

name: Woking
why: Green, safe and cheaper, with Horsell Common and the Basingstoke Canal. Two Outstanding primaries (St Hugh of Lincoln RC, 216, and Pyrford CofE) and a mid-sized secondary, Hoe Valley (892). Fast trains to Waterloo, but the commute is over 40 minutes and family is far.

name: St Albans
why: Cathedral city with a strong Catholic school network, at the edge of the commute limit.

name: Forest Gate
why: Next to Wanstead Flats and minutes from family in Wanstead, with the Elizabeth line to Liverpool Street (Moorgate exit) in about 12 minutes. Victorian terraces on the Woodgrange Estate and around Woodgrange Road. Small primaries (St James' CofE 190, William Davies 215, St Francis' RC 256) and an Exceptional secondary, Forest Gate Community School, but it has 1,343 pupils, and crime is the highest of the areas.

name: Leytonstone
why: Independent high street with Wanstead Flats and Epping Forest's Hollow Ponds close by. Two Outstanding primaries (Davies Lane, Newport) and small ones such as Dawlish (158) and Mayville (274); Leytonstone School (1,028) is the local secondary. Central line straight to the City.

name: Highams Park
why: Village feel on the edge of Epping Forest. Small Outstanding primaries (Oakhill 207, Selwyn) and two Good secondaries, Heathcote (1,115) and Highams Park (1,592). Weaver line trains to Liverpool Street.

name: Palmers Green & Winchmore Hill
why: Leafy suburb with Grovelands and Broomfield parks and the Green Lanes high street. Highlands (Outstanding) and Winchmore secondaries sit just outside the wards; only three state primaries inside them, more nearby. Direct trains to Moorgate from Palmers Green and Winchmore Hill.

name: Alexandra Park & Bowes Park
why: Alexandra Palace park and a Crouch End feel for less. Alexandra Park School (1,888, Outstanding) and small primaries such as St Martin of Porres (110) and Tottenhall Infant (204). Direct trains to Moorgate from Alexandra Palace and Bowes Park.

name: Stoke Newington
why: Independent shops, Clissold and Abney parks and the most bakeries and delis on the shortlist, but dense and busy. Outstanding primaries (Grazebrook, William Patten) and small ones such as Grasmere (220) and St Matthias (191). Overground to Liverpool Street; near the top of the budget.

name: Gidea Park
why: Quiet garden suburb by Raphael Park, the cheapest of the London options. Outstanding primaries (Nelmes, Ardleigh Green infant and junior); Emerson Park Academy (1,020) for secondary. Elizabeth line to Liverpool Street.

name: Brentwood
why: Essex market town with Thorndon and Weald country parks nearby, among the lowest prices on the shortlist. Becket Keys (Outstanding, CofE), Shenfield High and Brentwood County High for secondary; Shenfield St Mary's is an Outstanding primary. Elizabeth line from Brentwood and Shenfield.

name: Harringay & Green Lanes
why: Green Lanes is one of London's liveliest food streets, with the Victorian Harringay Ladder behind it and Finsbury Park at the end. Trains from Harringay run straight into Moorgate. Small primaries (South Harringay Junior 234 and St John Vianney RC 234, both Outstanding), but busy streets: crime is among the highest on the shortlist.

name: Leyton
why: Francis Road's independent cafés and shops, the Lea Valley marshes and the Olympic Park nearby, and minutes from family. Three Outstanding primaries (Riverley, Sybourn, Willow Brook) and tiny Catholic infant and junior schools (132 and 107); George Mitchell (973, ages 4–16) is the Good all-through school. Cheaper than Walthamstow and Leytonstone.

name: Clapton & Hackney Downs
why: Lively, creative and very mixed, with Hackney Downs, Millfields and the marshes, and the Overground to Liverpool Street in about 10 minutes. Outstanding primaries (Northwold, Southwold) and Mossbourne Community Academy (Exceptional) just outside, but houses are expensive and it is dense and busy.

name: Bow & Victoria Park
why: Roman Road's market and cafés, Victoria Park on the doorstep and the Central line at Mile End, a few stops from both the City and Wanstead. Old Ford Primary is Outstanding and Mossbourne Victoria Park Academy (838, Outstanding) is small for a London secondary; half the homes sold are in conservation areas. Crime is above the shortlist middle.

name: Tufnell Park & Archway
why: Victorian terraces between Tufnell Park, Archway and Whitehall Park, close to Hampstead Heath and the Parkland Walk. Outstanding primaries Yerbury (453) and St Joseph's (523, Catholic); the one secondary in the wards, Lift Beacon High (414), is small with a high free-meals share. Northern line straight to Moorgate.

name: Brockley & Honor Oak
why: Hilly Fields, Blythe Hill and One Tree Hill, with independent cafés, the Brockley market and the Jack theatre. Many Good or Outstanding primaries, such as Stillness, John Stainer and Haberdashers' Hatcham Free; secondaries are Haberdashers' Hatcham College (1,375) and the all-through Prendergast Ladywell (1,280). Overground, then the Elizabeth line at Whitechapel.

name: Acton
why: Acton High Street with Acton Green and the Bedford Park edge, one of the most mixed parts of west London. Outstanding Southfield and Ark Priory primaries and Ark Soane Academy (874, Outstanding). Elizabeth line from Acton Main Line; a long way from east London.

name: West Ealing & Hanwell
why: Edwardian family streets between West Ealing Broadway and Hanwell, with Brent River Park, Walpole Park and the canal. Outstanding Oaklands and St John's primaries and Drayton Manor High (1,443, Outstanding). Elizabeth line from West Ealing and Hanwell; a long way from east London.

name: Woodford Bridge & Woodford Green
why: Woodford Bridge's village green and Woodford Green, between Epping Forest and the Roding Valley, a short drive from family. Outstanding Churchfields Infants and Juniors (7% and 15% free meals) and Woodbridge High (1,980, Outstanding). Quieter, greener and cheaper than Wanstead, but few shops or cafés within walking distance; Central line from Woodford.
